messages.content:
You are identifying variation axes for AI risk concepts using ontology classes.

A variation axis is an ontology class that represents a dimension along which diverse prompts can be generated. Each axis has a semantic role relative to the risk:
- agent: Who performs or is affected by the action
- object: What is acted upon
- instrument: What tool/means is used
- location: Where it occurs
- temporal: When it occurs

Given a risk (with description and concern) and candidate ontology classes (with definitions and siblings), select the classes that are most semantically relevant to the risk.

Return 2-3 axes max.

Risk: Corporate liability
Description: The AI system's use may lead to legal action or penalties against corporations for intellectual property infringement, AI-related misconduct, violations of fiduciary duty, or failure to adequately oversee AI systems.
Concern: None
Policy: Executive Compensation

Candidate ontology classes:
- https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontology/FND/Law/LegalCore/Law: law — rule recognized by some community as regulating the behavior of its members and that it may enforce through the imposition of penalties [found by 2/4 queries]
- https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontology/LOAN/LoansGeneral/LoansRegulatory/InformationRight: information right — The right to some information in some context, for example when purchasing some product. The right to full and fair disclosure of
  Siblings: equal treatment right
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#HarmfulHowTo: Harmful How-To — Step-by-step instructions for activities that cause property destruction, physical harm, or enable illegal intrusion when executed by unauthorized individuals. [found by 3/4 queries]
  Siblings: CBRN Information, Drug Synthesis, Dual-Use Research Concern
- https://www.omg.org/spec/Commons/BusinessAuthorizations/Authorization: authorisation — situation in which a party authorizes someone to act on their behalf or to have specific capabilities under certain conditions for some period of time [found by 3/4 queries]
  Siblings: trade, ownership control situation, study
- https://www.omg.org/spec/Commons/RegulatoryAgencies/RegulatoryReport: regulatory report — document required to support operational transparency that demonstrates compliance with some specification, law, policy, restriction, or other rule specified by a regulatory agency [found by 3/4 queries]
  Siblings: technical specification document, registry, transaction record
- https://www.omg.org/spec/Commons/BusinessAuthorizations/AuthorizingParty: authorising party — party that delegates some role, authority, or control to another party [from restriction: hasAuthorizingParty on Authorization]
  Siblings: owner, registrar, controlling party
- https://www.omg.org/spec/Commons/BusinessAuthorizations/AuthorizedParty: authorised party — party that has been given the ability to act on behalf of another party or to have specified capabilities under some set of guidelines for some period of time [from restriction: hasAuthorizedParty on Authorization]
  Siblings: Occupation Role, Contractor Role, service provider

axes.rationale: The risk centers on 'legal action or penalties' and 'violations of fiduciary duty,' which directly relates to the concept of 'law' (a rule enforced by penalties). The corporation is the primary entity *subject* to this law, making it relevant as an agent/affected party.

The risk involves 'failure to adequately oversee AI systems' and violations of 'fiduciary duty.' In a corporate context, the board or senior management acts as the *Authorizing Party* (or responsible oversight body) that delegates authority but is ultimately liable for failures in supervision.

The AI system itself or the employees using it are the *Authorized Parties* acting on behalf of the corporation. The liability concern arises from their actions (or lack thereof) while operating under delegated authority.
